cases.scenario: Fetch own profile as an active, fully-onboarded seller returns 200 with the full profile DTO
cases.preconditions: Seller account with isSeller:true, suspended:false, sellerProfile set. ASSUMPTION: ST_USER is the configured seller/owner account (per run.ps1 inline doc '-Role user # one endpoint as the seller/user account', and fixtures.json _owners using ST_USER as the listing-creating account, which requires seller permission). fixtures.json does NOT independently record each account's isSeller/suspended/sellerProfile state - verify before running; see audit Test design inputs (h).
cases.response_assertions: body.shopName exists; body.isSeller == true; body.payout exists or is null; body.suspended is absent; body.status is absent
cases.business_outcome: Active, onboarded sellers can load their own Seller Hub / dashboard profile data
cases.expected: 200 with full profile DTO (shopName, shopTagline, shopLogo, phoneNumber, sellerCategories, address fields, sellerType, legalName, taxIdLast4, notifyFollowersOnNewListing, payout, isSeller); no suspended/status field exists in the contract
cases.source: audit EP-109 suggested scenario #1; Declared Contract section; sellers.service.ts:495-524

cases.scenario: Logged-in non-seller USER (buyer, isSeller:false) calling GET /sellers/me gets 403 Insufficient permissions
cases.preconditions: Needs a confirmed non-seller USER account (isSeller:false). conftest.py/fixtures.json only define owner(ST_USER)/other(ST_USER2)/admin(ST_ADMIN) without documenting which of these are sellers; audit's own fixture-needs list (item h) calls for a dedicated non-seller USER account that is not currently recorded.
cases.test_data: No confirmed non-seller USER credentials recorded - fixture gap
cases.steps: GET /sellers/me with Authorization: Bearer <non-seller USER token>
cases.business_outcome: RolesGuard live-checks isSeller (not the stale JWT claim) and rejects any non-seller caller
cases.blocked_reason: No confirmed non-seller USER account exists in fixtures.json/conftest.py (ST_USER2/'other' account's isSeller status is undocumented) - cannot execute until a dedicated non-seller buyer account is added and its credentials configured as ST_USER2.

cases.scenario: Pre-existing valid JWT; account suspended mid-session via admin action; replaying the old token on GET /sellers/me returns 401 'Account suspended.' - NOT 200, no profile body, no status field to inspect
cases.preconditions: Needs a dedicated, disposable seller account to suspend (not ST_USER/ST_ADMIN, which must stay unsuspended for other tests) plus an admin JWT to call PATCH /admin/users/:id/suspend. No such fixture exists in fixtures.json/conftest.py/factory.py today.
cases.test_data: Dedicated seller fixture needed: mint a JWT as that seller, then admin suspends via PATCH /admin/users/:id/suspend, then replay the pre-suspension JWT against GET /sellers/me
cases.steps: 1) Login as a disposable seller, capture JWT. 2) As admin, PATCH /admin/users/:id/suspend for that seller. 3) GET /sellers/me with the step-1 (pre-suspension) JWT
cases.response_assertions: body.message == 'Account suspended.'; response contains no profile fields at all (no 200 path exists)
cases.business_outcome: Suspension is enforced at the auth layer (JwtStrategy.validate), live from the DB, before SellersController.getProfile ever runs - a suspended seller can never reach a 200 from this endpoint
cases.expected: 401 'Account suspended.', confirming Finding #1 (not 200 with a visible status)
cases.blocked_reason: No dedicated/disposable suspended-seller fixture exists; requires an admin JWT to create one via PATCH /admin/users/:id/suspend (admin.controller.ts:160-165) using an account other than the shared ST_USER/ST_ADMIN test accounts, plus a way to capture a pre-suspension JWT for replay.
cases.source: audit EP-109 suggested scenario #4; jwt.strategy.ts:34-62 (:42); apiClient.refresh.test.ts:119-124

cases.scenario: Sheet-title-literal scenario: 'a suspended seller's own profile view clearly reflects the suspended status' - cannot be given a trustworthy expected result as written
cases.preconditions: Structurally impossible under shipped code: JwtStrategy.validate (jwt.strategy.ts:42) throws 401 'Account suspended.' before SellersController.getProfile ever runs, for any suspended account; even hypothetically bypassing that gate, getProfile()'s response DTO (sellers.service.ts:500-523) has no suspended/status field at all (contrast getAllSellers/getSellerByIdForAdmin, which do have one).
cases.steps: N/A - cannot be executed as the sheet literally describes it: there is no success path where a suspended seller reaches a 200 profile view to inspect for a suspended indicator
cases.expected: Per sheet title: 200 with a visible suspended indicator. Per shipped code: 401, no body, no indicator exists anywhere in the contract. Do NOT assert a 200-with-status-field as pass/fail until PO/QA clarifies intent.
cases.business_outcome: Sheet row's premise conflicts with the shipped account-suspension design (login/auth-layer block, not a profile-view state). Needs a product/QA decision: keep current behaviour (block before profile) vs. build a genuinely new capability (let a suspended seller log in and see a 'Suspended' banner on their own profile).
cases.blocked_reason: CF-109-01: sheet title requires a suspended seller to see a 200 profile response reflecting 'suspended' status; code structurally prevents any suspended account from reaching a 200 on this endpoint (auth-layer 401 first, jwt.strategy.ts:42), and the response DTO has no suspended/status field even if that gate were bypassed (sellers.service.ts:500-523). Needs PO/QA decision on intended behaviour before this can be tested as written.
cases.source: audit EP-109 suggested scenario #7; Source agreement matrix rows 1-2; Sheet Check section

cases.scenario: No cross-account access vector exists on this route - there is no :id path param, so 'ownership' is definitionally the caller themselves
cases.preconditions: Route declares zero path/query params; req.user.id from the JWT is the only input (sellers.controller.ts:127-133)
cases.steps: Code-review confirmation: GET /sellers/me takes no target-user input of any kind; documents the absence of an IDOR risk class on this specific route rather than a request to execute
cases.expected: Confirmed absence of an IDOR surface - there is no way to request another user's seller profile via this endpoint (contrast GET /sellers/:userId/shop, a separate, intentionally public endpoint)

cases.scenario: Unknown/extra query params (e.g. ?foo=bar) sent to GET /sellers/me are ignored; response unaffected
cases.expected: 200, unknown query params ignored, no validation error, no behaviour change

cases.scenario: Malformed/expired/tampered JWT on GET /sellers/me returns 401, no 500/leak
cases.preconditions: Needs a literal invalid-signature token and/or a known-expired token string - not mintable via the harness's normal login flow (hooks.py RoleAuth only logs in a real account or sends no token at all; it cannot inject an arbitrary garbage Authorization header)
cases.test_data: Authorization: Bearer <garbage/tampered JWT>; and a known-expired JWT if available
cases.response_assertions: no 5xx; standard 401 body; no internal error/stack-trace leak
cases.expected: 401, no 500, no leaked internals (pinned HS256 algorithm in jwt.strategy.ts)

cases.scenario: Session revoked via 'sid' check (e.g. sign out all devices) then retry GET /sellers/me with the old token - 401 with a message distinct from suspension
cases.preconditions: Needs a mechanism to revoke a session's sid (e.g. a 'sign out all devices' endpoint/call) - not scripted anywhere in factory.py/conftest.py; no fixture or helper for this exists in the harness today
cases.test_data: Owner JWT + a way to revoke its sid
cases.steps: 1) Login as seller, capture JWT. 2) Trigger session revocation (sign out all devices / sid invalidation). 3) GET /sellers/me with the old (now-revoked) JWT
cases.response_assertions: body.message == 'Session ended. Please sign in again.' - must be distinct from 'Account suspended.'
cases.business_outcome: Confirms the 401 reason/message for a revoked session differs from a suspended account, which matters for any client-side error-message mapping that tries to distinguish the two
cases.blocked_reason: No scripted mechanism/fixture exists in this harness to revoke a session's sid (no 'sign out all devices' call in factory.py/conftest.py) - cannot execute until one is added
